quiz.question: What happens when synchronous code encounters a long-running task like a network request?

answers.answer: It skips the task and moves to the next line
It blocks and waits for the task to finish before continuing
It runs the task in the background automatically
It throws an error because synchronous code cannot do network requests

quiz.explanation: Synchronous code runs line by line. Each line must finish before the next one starts, so a long-running task blocks everything after it until it completes.

quiz.question: Why is asynchronous code important for I/O operations like fetching data?

answers.answer: It makes the data arrive faster from the server
It prevents your program from freezing while waiting for a response
It guarantees the data will always be available

quiz.explanation: Asynchronous code lets your program kick off a task like a network request and keep running other code while waiting for the result, preventing the program from freezing.
